dct_title_s: Nepal Flood 2026 River Corridor, Bhote Koshi and Trishuli
dct_description_sm: OpenStreetMap and Overture Maps vector layers for the full Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river corridor in Bagmati and Gandaki Provinces, Nepal, for the 2026 flood response. The area of interest is a 1 km buffer around the river centrelines, covering 317.51 square kilometres, running from Rasuwagadhi on the China border to the Narayani confluence at Devghat in Chitwan. It crosses six districts, Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha, Tanahu and Chitawan, and twenty municipalities. The corridor merges the original partner shapefile for the upper reach with OCHA's HPCS 1 km corridor for the downstream reach. This is the wide planning view: it covers the whole corridor under assessment, not only the ground that flooded. **For data limited to the area that actually flooded, use [Nepal Flood 2026 Flood Affected Area](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/hot_flood_npl),** which clips every layer to the observed inundation footprint of 27 August 2026 and a 200 m margin around it. Buildings mappers have recorded as destroyed are in a separate **Destroyed Buildings** layer. The `destroyed:` prefix replaces the plain `building` tag, so these are not in the Buildings layer. Read both together for the building stock before the flood. Every layer is published here as a resource, and most layers carry two versions, one from OpenStreetMap and one from Overture Maps. The two are not interchangeable: - **OpenStreetMap** layers are live. They are rebuilt daily from the latest OSM data, so they pick up work by volunteer mappers as the response progresses. Use these when currency matters. - **Overture Maps** layers fuse building footprints and other features from Microsoft, Google and OpenStreetMap. That fusion gives broader coverage than OSM alone in places volunteers have not reached yet, but **Overture is not updated daily**. It follows Overture's own release cycle, so it will not reflect mapping done during this response and will fall progressively further behind the OpenStreetMap layers. In short, Overture is wider but older; OpenStreetMap is current. For damage assessment against the latest mapping, prefer the OpenStreetMap layers and treat Overture as a supplement where OSM coverage is thin. Mapping task boundaries from the Tasking Manager campaign are published here too and refreshed daily, showing where volunteers are being asked to map. The bridge damage assessment is reported from the ground by volunteers. It lists road bridges with their condition after the flood, deck length where measured, and administrative codes from the same boundaries as the other layers. - Source: [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/), [Overture Maps](https://overturemaps.org/), volunteer field reports - Part of HOT disaster response exports on HDX by [HOT](https://www.hotosm.org/)
dct_publisher_sm: OpenStreetMap contributors, Overture Maps, volunteer field reports
